articles.title: Banana Republic debuts TikTok content series in bid for younger shoppers
articles.summary: Banana Republic debuted its first channel-first original content series, "The Agency," on TikTok on Oct. 14, marking a push into entertainment marketing aimed at younger shoppers. Produced by Banana Republic Productions, the five-part series stars Jack Innanen playing multiple employees at a struggling fictional New York travel agency called Travel & Tours, alongside Taylor Ortega as a corporate consultant sent to modernize the business and Milo Tucker-Meyer as an intern. Each character's wardrobe highlights different Banana Republic collections and fabrics. The premiere episode, "The Fax," introduced the eccentric staff and has drawn over 10 million views, while episode two topped 3 million views within its first week. CMO Meena Anvary framed the project as a nod to the brand's storytelling roots dating back to its 1978 founding by a journalist and illustrator. The launch follows Gap Inc.'s broader "Fashiontainment" strategy, which included hiring former Paramount executive Pam Kaufman as chief entertainment officer and a September partnership between the Gap brand and boy band Just Your Type. Banana Republic posted 3% comparable sales growth in Q2 2026, compared to 10% growth at Gap and a 12% decline at Athleta.
articles.li_summary: Banana Republic launched "The Agency," a five-episode TikTok series starring Jack Innanen as staff at a fictional travel agency, debuting Oct. 14 with over 10 million views on episode one.

articles.title: Meta says shopping is Muse’s primary use case
articles.summary: Meta disclosed new details about its Muse AI agent during its Q3 earnings call, revealing more than 10 million downloads since launching in the US and Canada last month, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg noting it has topped App Store charts almost daily and that roughly 25% of users engage with it daily. Shopping emerged as the dominant use case, with over 25% of users seeking deals or making purchases averaging more than $200 each, prompting Meta to work with Stripe to raise credit limits after transaction volumes exceeded expectations in the first week, while Plaid reported unprecedented activity through its payment connector. Third-party data from Sensor Tower suggests retention drops sharply after two weeks, a pattern common across AI chatbots. Zuckerberg outlined plans for a "Muse network" allowing personal AI agents to collaborate with friends, family, and business agents directly, plus a new "Confidential VM" to address privacy concerns following a cybersecurity group's exposure of user query data and a separate $25 billion New Mexico privacy ruling against Meta. Muse is expected on Meta glasses starting November.
articles.li_summary: Meta revealed Muse AI agent has surpassed 10 million downloads since its September launch in the US and Canada, with shopping as the top use case, driving average purchases over $200 per transaction.

articles.title: Meta offers insights on individual platform growth
articles.summary: Meta's Q3 2026 earnings update included platform-specific growth details relevant to marketers. CFO Susan Li said Instagram reached all-time-high time spent per user, with Reels relevance updates boosting watch time over 4% after shifting to a model that ranks sequences of Reels together rather than individually; nearly 45% of recommended Reels are now under a day old, up 11 points from Q2, meaning most engagement now happens within 24 hours of posting. On Facebook, Reels time spent also hit an all-time high, growing double-digit percentages year over year, helped by a new generative retrieval architecture inspired by LLMs that labels content semantically to surface fresh posts faster; it's now live across roughly a quarter of unconnected Feed views and half of Reels views, lifting Reels watch time 1%, with a doubled historical ranking window adding another 1% gain in the US. CEO Mark Zuckerberg confirmed Threads has surpassed X in monthly active users, now exceeding 500 million, with time spent per user up more than 20% year over year. Meta also opened its Creator Marketing Hub, featuring 10 million-plus creators, to all advertisers, and is adding AI-powered conversational search for creator partnerships.
articles.li_summary: Meta's Q3 2026 earnings commentary revealed Instagram and Facebook Reels hit all-time-high time spent, Threads overtook X in monthly active users with over 500 million MAUs, and Meta's Creator Marketing Hub now lists 10 million-plus creators for advertisers.

articles.title: Snapchat says some AI users are willing to trade privacy for utility
articles.summary: Snapchat has released a report examining shifting attitudes toward AI chatbots, drawing on a survey of more than 4,200 AI users conducted with Ipsos and WPP. The findings show 48% of consumers now use AI daily, while 50% of creators and marketers consider it central to their workflow. Sixty-two percent said AI tools help them sustain conversations and think through ideas, and over 80% described AI as friendly and collaborative; 74% see it as a judgment-free space for privately working through complex emotions before discussing them with others. Snapchat users specifically were found 2.2 times more likely to say AI benefits their social life and 1.6 times more likely to use it for planning real-world activities. The report frames privacy as a flexible "sliding scale," arguing users will share data when the personalization payoff feels worthwhile, particularly for conversational AI. However, this same audience remains wary of AI managing money or purchases, and the report notes 70% find AI-personalized ads intrusive while 56% view fully AI-generated content as "soulless," revealing a split between comfort with private AI assistance and discomfort with AI-driven marketing and content.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat's new report, based on an Ipsos/WPP survey of over 4,200 AI users, finds 48% use AI daily and that many will trade personal data for personalized AI value, though 70% still call AI-driven ad targeting intrusive.

articles.title: Meta hit with $25 billion fine over privacy breaches
articles.summary: A New Mexico court has fined Meta $25 billion following a jury verdict that found the company violated users' privacy and knowingly allowed harmful content to remain on Facebook when it served business interests. The case centers on the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal, where millions of users' data was accessed without consent by a political consulting firm, an incident Meta executive Andrew Bosworth once dismissed as a "non-event." New Mexico's attorney general argued Meta misled users about third-party data access and tolerated hate speech and misinformation for profit. The judge noted that state law actually justified a much larger $219 billion penalty but settled on $25 billion instead. This case was pursued separately from a broader 52-state coalition effort that resulted in an $18 billion settlement with Meta in August over child safety failures. Meta's Chief Legal Officer C.J. Mahoney called the ruling harmful to businesses operating in the state and confirmed the company will appeal. The penalty adds to Meta's mounting legal troubles worldwide and raises fresh doubts about its data practices as it pushes users to share more personal information with its new Muse AI assistants.
articles.li_summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found it liable for privacy breaches tied to the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal and for knowingly exposing users to harmful content, with Meta vowing to appeal.

articles.title: LinkedIn publishes new guide to B2B conversion tracking
articles.summary: LinkedIn has published a new 18-page guide aimed at helping B2B marketers better connect early buyer engagement signals to ad performance and investment decisions. The guide addresses the complexity of B2B buying journeys, which often involve multiple stakeholders, anonymous research, content consumption without clicks, and growing use of AI tools, all of which make traditional attribution models unreliable. LinkedIn cites internal research showing only 33% of B2B marketers strongly agree they can demonstrate marketing's impact to their C-suite, while 75% admit their current measurement systems are inadequate. To address this gap, the guide lays out five practical frameworks for tracking promotional performance, along with detailed steps for each. It also includes guidance on achieving "full-funnel visibility" across the buyer journey and a curated list of LinkedIn-approved attribution and analytics partners marketers can integrate for added context. While the resource offers genuinely useful, actionable steps for improving campaign tracking on LinkedIn, it also serves as a promotional tool highlighting the platform's own analytics products, some of which require a paid subscription to access.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn released an 18-page B2B ads attribution guide with five measurement frameworks, citing data that only 33% of B2B marketers can prove marketing impact to their C-suite while 75% say their tracking systems fall short.

articles.title: Domino’s links with Minecraft to push personal pizza via gaming
articles.summary: Domino's is partnering with "Minecraft Dungeons II," the video game released Sept. 29, in a campaign launching Oct. 26 across 19 global markets to promote its new Domino personal pizza, which debuted Aug. 31 and is positioned for gaming-session meal occasions. Domino's Rewards members who buy a Domino can unlock exclusive in-game items, including an avatar skin, a cape and a Cheesy Cube Pet companion, marking the game's first co-branded partnership pet; the loyalty program closed 2025 with over 37 million active users, up nearly 20% since its 2023 relaunch. From Oct. 26 through Nov. 4, Domino's will give away 2,000 game-download tokens daily, with customers submitting purchase proof on a microsite for entry, helping the chain gather first-party data from non-members too. The push also features VFX creators Merrick Hanna, Daphne Le, JoshVFX and the Macfarlane Brothers across social and a 15-second TV spot, plus six collectible Minecraft-character boxes and an upcoming game-themed redesign of the Domino's Tracker. This follows Domino's earlier gaming tie-ins, including Twitch's Fortnite network and reviving its Noid character.
articles.li_summary: Domino's launches an Oct. 26 "Minecraft Dungeons II" collaboration across 19 global markets, offering in-game rewards, 2,000 daily free game-download tokens through Nov. 4, and VFX-creator content tied to its new rectangular Domino personal pizza.

articles.title: Meta offers creative ad targeting for specific audiences
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out a new Marketing API feature allowing third-party platforms and marketers to attach audience targeting details, specifically age range and gender, to individual creative elements like images and videos, rather than applying those parameters only at the ad set level. This means a financial services brand could designate retirement-planning videos for users aged 50 to 65 while keeping savings account content open to all ages, or a fashion retailer could point women's sweater images toward female users and men's sweater images toward male users. By embedding targeting instructions directly into the creative, Meta's ad delivery system can more precisely match specific visuals to specific users, potentially boosting relevance without marketers needing to build separate campaigns for each demographic slice. The change took effect this week. One possible complication is gift-buying behavior, especially heading into the holiday shopping season, since restricting creative by gender or age could limit visibility to people purchasing items for someone outside that target group, raising questions about how this might affect overall campaign reach and conversions during peak shopping periods.
articles.li_summary: Meta updated its Marketing API this week to let advertisers assign specific age-range and gender targeting directly to individual ad creatives rather than entire ad sets, aiming to improve visual relevance for each user shown an ad.

articles.title: Meta adds users and revenue as AI costs climb
articles.summary: Meta's Q3 earnings showed continued ad strength alongside ballooning AI costs: daily active users across its apps grew by 40 million to 3.64 billion, with India now its largest market and Asia-Pacific ad impressions up 24% this year, while overall ad impressions rose 10% and ad prices climbed 14%, pushing revenue up 26% year-over-year to $64.6 billion. However, expenses jumped 68% year-over-year, largely from capital expenditures tied to Meta's AI buildout, which includes a previously announced $600 million-plus infrastructure commitment. Reality Labs revenue barely moved quarter-over-quarter, with AI glasses sales reportedly slowing amid misuse backlash, leaving Meta's Muse AI agent as a key hope for future monetization through transaction fees. Muse faces its own troubles
articles.li_summary: Meta's Q3 revenue climbed 26% year-over-year to $64.6 billion and daily active users reached 3.64 billion, even as AI infrastructure spending drove a 68% jump in expenses and headcount fell 15% to 66,775.

articles.title: YouTube shares data on how creators are using AI
articles.summary: YouTube released a new installment of its Culture & Trends series examining how creators incorporate AI into content creation, commissioning research firm NRG to survey almost 700 people aged 14 to 44 who had posted video online within the past year. The standout finding: 72% of these uploaders reported using AI on videos or images, while 61% expressed interest in using AI to digitally insert themselves into content, making this the most common use case among those who had already created AI videos, with over two-thirds confirming they'd featured themselves this way. Examples cited include people recasting themselves as doctors, judges, or superheroes through "digital costume changes," designers using AI to visualize fashion concepts, creators placing themselves inside video game scenes, and a growing group of "AI auteurs" constructing entire cinematic universes from imagination. YouTube frames this as creative empowerment, though the report acknowledges tension between legitimate storytelling innovation and risks like misinformation or misleading depictions, alongside broader concerns about low-quality "AI slop" flooding the platform.
articles.li_summary: YouTube's new Culture & Trends report, based on an NRG survey of nearly 700 video uploaders aged 14-44, found 72% use AI tools on videos or images, with 61% specifically interested in inserting themselves into AI-generated content.

articles.title: YouTube adds temporary pause for hacked accounts
articles.summary: YouTube has introduced an automated temporary pause feature designed to protect creators from account hijacking. When the platform detects unusual or unauthorized activity on a channel, it will immediately restrict several functions: uploading new content, starting livestreams, adding videos to playlists, creating custom thumbnails, and switching videos between private, unlisted, and public settings. This is meant to stop hackers from quickly locking out real owners and posting unwanted videos or streams. During the pause, YouTube's security team reviews the account, typically within 24 hours; if ownership is verified, full access returns immediately, and if hacking is confirmed, YouTube contacts the creator with recovery steps. Importantly, viewers can still watch and engage with existing channel content during the restriction, and monetization remains unaffected. Affected creators will see a notification banner inside YouTube Studio explaining the restriction, with a link to more details about the suspicious activity and guidance on recovering the account. The update adds a layer of security for creators who have invested years building audiences and revenue streams on the platform.
articles.li_summary: YouTube now automatically pauses uploads, livestreams, playlist edits, and thumbnail changes on channels showing suspicious activity, with security teams reviewing flagged accounts within 24 hours to restore or secure access.

articles.title: Meta shares more information on Edits Plus subscriptions
articles.summary: Meta has shared new details on Edits Plus, a paid subscription tier for its Edits video editing app that it first previewed last month alongside broader plans for add-on subscriptions. The package will unlock additional cloud storage and increased access to AI-powered creation tools, available to users with Instagram personal or professional creator accounts who sign up directly through the Edits mobile app. So far, Meta has confirmed only one specific benefit: 200GB of cloud storage, which lets creators sync, back up, and access editing projects across multiple devices on the same operating system, such as between iOS devices or between Android devices. Pricing has not yet been disclosed, and the subscription will initially roll out through limited testing rather than a full launch. Instagram chief Adam Mosseri has previously indicated that monetizing Edits was inevitable given the rising computing costs tied to running AI features, and Meta is expected to expand Edits Plus with additional perks over time to encourage more creators to subscribe.
articles.li_summary: Meta detailed its upcoming Edits Plus subscription, which will offer 200GB of cloud storage and expanded AI tool usage within the Edits mobile app, though pricing remains unannounced ahead of limited testing.

articles.title: Domino’s links with Minecraft to push personal pizza via gaming
articles.summary: Domino's is partnering with "Minecraft Dungeons II" starting Oct. 26, connecting the campaign to its Detroit-style "Domino" personal pizza that launched Aug. 31, whose rectangular shape mirrors Minecraft's block aesthetic. Domino's Rewards members who buy a Domino can unlock exclusive in-game items, including an avatar skin, a cape, and a Cheesy Cube Pet, marking the game's first co-branded companion pet. The loyalty program, which grew to over 37 million active users in 2025 (up nearly 20% since its 2023 relaunch), is central to the promotion. From Oct. 26 to Nov. 4, Domino's will give away 2,000 game-download tokens daily to customers who purchase a Domino and submit proof via a microsite, also helping the brand gather first-party data from non-members. The campaign includes six collectible packaging designs featuring in-game characters and an upcoming interactive, game-themed redesign of the Domino's Tracker. Creators including Merrick Hanna, Daphne Le, JoshVFX, and the MacFarlane Brothers will produce social content, with the MacFarlane Brothers also starring in a 15-second TV spot. The collaboration will run across 19 global markets, with rollout details varying by region.
articles.li_summary: Domino's launches an Oct. 26 "Minecraft Dungeons II" tie-in across 19 markets, offering in-game items, 2,000 daily free game tokens through Nov. 4, and six collectible pizza boxes tied to its new rectangular Domino pizza.

articles.title: TikTok shares Black Friday/Cyber Monday promotion tips
articles.summary: TikTok has released a "Road to Black Friday" video series spotlighting three brands' strategies for driving holiday sales through TikTok Shop. Fashion retailer Princess Polly partners with hundreds of creators monthly and generated roughly 6,000 TikTok Shop creator videos in a single month, while fragrance brand Dossier works with thousands of creators, has over 80,000 videos live, and sends samples to between 1,000 and 5,000 creators each month. Appliance brand SharkNinja leans on TikTok Live to field shopper questions, collect feedback, and fine-tune content performance in real time. TikTok's accompanying data makes the case for this investment: #holidayshopping content jumped 263% month-over-month in September 2026, TikTok Shop listings surfaced in more than 100 billion U.S. searches with purchase intent during 2025, and last year's Black Friday/Cyber Monday weekend generated over $500 million in TikTok Shop sales. Sellers who ran livestreams saw 84% year-over-year sales growth, signaling TikTok's push to position Live shopping as a core holiday sales driver for brands this season.
articles.li_summary: TikTok launched a "Road to Black Friday" video series highlighting how Dossier, Princess Polly, and SharkNinja use TikTok Shop, creator partnerships, and Live streams, with holiday shopping content up 263% month-over-month in September 2026.

articles.title: Australia prepares to sue social platforms over age violations
articles.summary: Australia is moving toward legal action against major social platforms for failing to enforce its under-16 social media ban, which took effect in December 2025 as the world's first law of its kind. Communications Minister Anika Wells, who also serves as the nation's online safety regulator, confirmed she is collecting evidence for federal court proceedings against Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube. While platforms reported removing or suspending hundreds of thousands of suspected underage accounts after the law passed, early data suggested most young users still found ways to access these apps. The regulations require platforms to take "reasonable steps" to block underage users, but the vague wording leaves room for companies to contest liability, and the government has not specified which enforcement methods count as sufficient. To strengthen pressure on noncompliant platforms, Australia recently doubled the maximum penalty for violations to $70 million per breach. With legal action now looming, platforms may face stronger incentive to adopt more rigorous and verifiable age-verification systems rather than risk costly court battles and reputational damage.
articles.li_summary: Australia’s government is preparing to sue Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube for failing to keep under-16 users off their platforms, with Communications Minister Anika Wells gathering evidence for federal court action and fines now doubled to $70 million per breach.

articles.title: Instagram announces next phase of Rings creative talent awards
articles.summary: Instagram has detailed the next phase of its Rings program, a creator recognition initiative first launched in October 2025 to spotlight creative talent that shapes broader cultural trends rather than just producing viral content. For 2026, winners will be chosen by a panel of 14 industry judges, including fashion designer Donatella Versace and musician A$AP Rocky, who will evaluate creators based on originality, creative risk-taking, and cultural impact rather than follower counts alone. Selected winners will receive in-app promotion through custom profile design features that highlight their status, plus a physical gold ring crafted by jewelry designer Emily Adams Bode Aujla as a tangible symbol of recognition. Notably, the program doesn't allow public or community nominations, with selections made entirely by the judging panel, which keeps the process somewhat opaque and limits audience participation compared to typical creator award shows. Still, Instagram frames Rings as a way to honor the broader creative process, including setbacks and experimentation, not just finished output, positioning it as a tool to retain and motivate the platform's most original, culture-shaping creators.
articles.li_summary: Instagram unveiled its 2026 Rings creator awards, judged by a 14-person panel including Donatella Versace and A$AP Rocky, with winners receiving in-app profile promotion and a custom gold ring by designer Emily Adams Bode Aujla.

articles.title: YouTube inks affiliate deal with AliExpress
articles.summary: YouTube has partnered with AliExpress to bring the China-based retailer into its shopping affiliate program, which launched in 2022 and allows creators to tag eligible products in their videos to earn commissions on resulting sales. The collaboration begins in South Korea in March 2026, then expands to four additional markets: the United States, Brazil, the United Kingdom, and Germany, with further rollout tied to YouTube's broader affiliate program expansion, which aims to reach 35 markets by the end of 2026 following a UK launch in August and announcements at YouTube's Made On event. Creators will be able to tag AliExpress products across multiple categories, using bestseller and trending-item data to select products suited to their audiences, with viewers able to click directly from YouTube videos to AliExpress to complete purchases. AliExpress lists over 100 million products and has seen rapid growth, including a 50% year-over-year increase in U.S. gross merchandise value during its May 2026 promotional period, making this partnership potentially lucrative for both creators seeking new income streams and AliExpress seeking expanded reach.
articles.li_summary: YouTube added AliExpress to its creator shopping affiliate program, letting eligible creators tag products in videos and earn commissions, starting in South Korea in March 2026 before expanding to the US, UK, Brazil, and Germany.

articles.title: Reddit adds AI-powered ad guidance tools
articles.summary: Reddit has introduced new AI-driven features within its Ads Manager to help advertisers plan and optimize campaigns more efficiently. The campaign planner lets advertisers input campaign details and generate forecasts covering reach, impressions, and estimated costs before launch, alongside data on target audience activity levels and summaries of trending conversation themes within relevant subreddits. A second feature, the campaign optimization score, rates campaigns on a 0-100% scale with tailored recommendations for improvement; Reddit reports that campaigns scoring 80% or above achieved a 19.6% lower blended cost-per-acquisition compared to those scoring lower. The third addition, campaign budget optimization, automatically redistributes ad spend across ad groups, shifting more budget toward top-performing groups to maximize overall returns. Together, these tools aim to reduce the manual research and guesswork traditionally required to run effective Reddit ad campaigns, potentially making the platform more appealing to advertisers who previously found it difficult to gauge performance. Reddit confirmed that the campaign planner and optimization score tools are being rolled out to all advertisers throughout October, with budget optimization also now available as part of the broader Ads Manager update.
articles.li_summary: Reddit rolled out three AI tools in Ads Manager this October—campaign planner, optimization score, and budget optimization—with campaigns scoring 80%+ showing 19.6% lower blended CPA than lower-scoring ones.

articles.title: Amy’s Kitchen tackles ultra-processed food myths in national campaign
articles.summary: Amy's Kitchen, the privately owned frozen and canned food maker founded in 1988, has launched a national marketing campaign aimed at correcting misconceptions about ultra-processed foods, timed to its recent Non-UPF Verified certification from the Non-GMO Project covering nearly 90% of its product lineup. The five-week effort, running through November 15 and targeting health-conscious consumers aged 24-44, launched in early October with a 40-foot "End the Era of Ultra-Processed Food" projection onto Santa Monica's Clock Tower Building. The campaign spans Meta and programmatic display ads, MikMak retargeting with add-to-cart functionality, and an in-store Whole Foods Market activation starting October 15 featuring digital ads and Amazon DSP targeting, plus freezer clings, shelf talkers, and print materials. Backing the push, a Northwestern University health economist's analysis commissioned by Amy's found diets high in ultra-processed foods carry $359,836 in additional lifetime economic burden, countering assumptions that such foods are cheaper. A companion Talker Research survey of 2,000 Americans found 90% unknowingly eat ultra-processed foods, half can't distinguish processed from ultra-processed, and nearly half mistakenly view frozen foods as unhealthy as chips or cookies—confusion Amy's hopes its new certification and messaging will resolve.
articles.li_summary: Amy's Kitchen launched a national five-week campaign through Nov. 15, highlighting its Non-UPF Verified certification for nearly 90% of products, using Meta ads, a Santa Monica Clock Tower projection, and Whole Foods in-store activations.

articles.title: Billion Dollar Boy Group bets B2B is creator marketing’s next big wave
articles.summary: London-based Billion Dollar Boy Group has completed its acquisition of Creator Authority, a three-year-old Santa Monica agency specializing in B2B creator and influencer marketing, with deal terms undisclosed. Creator Authority, a LinkedIn marketing partner, brings clients including Amazon, Adobe, AT&T, IBM, Dropbox, HubSpot, Mastercard and Notion, and will expand BDB Group's U.S. footprint beyond its existing New York office. CEO Ed East called B2B one of creator marketing's biggest growth areas, citing BDB Group survey data showing one-fifth of marketing decision-makers have invested in B2B creator campaigns this year, making it the second-most popular creator economy investment tracked. LinkedIn research cited in the announcement found 59% of B2B buyers engage with creator content on the platform, more than any other social network. Creator Authority co-founder Brendan Gahan, previously of Epic Signal, becomes BDB Group's senior vice president of B2B, while co-founder Cassie Jackson takes the role of group account director for B2B from Austin. BDB Group is aiming to surpass $100 million in global revenue next year as it deepens its U.S. investment.
articles.li_summary: Billion Dollar Boy Group acquired B2B-focused creator marketing agency Creator Authority, whose clients include Amazon, Adobe and Mastercard, to expand West Coast presence as it targets $100 million in global revenue next year.

articles.title: How marketers can optimize their media mix as confidence takes a turn
articles.summary: Kantar's 2026 Media Reactions report, surveying 806 senior marketers and 23,452 consumers across 33 markets between May and September, reveals declining advertiser confidence in media strategy: only 57% believe they have the right media mix, down from 64% in 2025, while just 51% feel they're getting actionable intelligence from their data. Confidence in balancing brand-building with performance marketing fell to 50% from 60% a year ago. Kantar Americas CEO Jeff Greenspoon attributes this not to lost faith in media but to a fragmenting ecosystem that's outgrowing decades-old decision-making models, with disconnected dashboards across media, creative, and commerce teams measuring individual channels rather than overall impact. Despite the uncertainty, marketers are doubling down on new bets: nearly two-thirds expect generative AI to shape brand recommendations, and 75% plan to increase AI assistant investment next year, though only 23% of consumers currently trust AI recommendations. Creator strategy is also shifting toward smaller influencers, with planned spending increases of 66% for micro-creators and 61% for nano-creators, compared to 42-48% increases for larger creators, as brands prioritize relevance over reach.
articles.li_summary: Kantar's 2026 Media Reactions report shows advertiser confidence in their media mix dropped to 57% from 64% last year, even as marketers boost spending 66% on micro-creators and 75% plan increased AI assistant investment.

articles.title: How Marriott Bonvoy got scale, speed with global creator-led campaign
articles.summary: Marriott Bonvoy debuted a new global brand platform last month, moving away from traditional ad production to a creator-led model built for speed and scale. Working with Beautiful Destinations, an agency with over 50 million followers and a network of 650+ creators, Marriott went from campaign brief to delivered assets in four weeks, capturing content across 10 countries, 23 destinations, and 14 hotel brands. The campaign launched in September with more than 1,600 out-of-home placements globally, running through year-end alongside in-flight entertainment, while social content continues into 2027. Marriott is targeting Q4 travel season, citing Nielsen data showing 71% of travelers think about their next trip at the airport and 77% take action after seeing airport ads. SVP of global marketing Behnaz Ghahramani said the creative direction favored an intimate, unpolished aesthetic over traditional overproduced ads. The push comes as Bonvoy surpassed 300 million members, with Marriott positioning the program as relational rather than transactional ahead of the company's 100th anniversary in 2027.
articles.li_summary: Marriott Bonvoy launched its new global brand platform "Wherever life's journey takes you, we'll see you there" by partnering with agency Beautiful Destinations' 650-creator network to produce campaign content across 10 countries, 23 destinations and 14 hotel brands in just four weeks.

articles.title: Anthropologie’s holiday marketing seeks to balance emotion, business impact
articles.summary: Anthropologie unveiled its 2025 holiday marketing strategy on Monday, anchored by an in-house campaign called "On My Way" filmed at Shelter Island, Mallorca and Vienna, depicting travelers reuniting with loved ones at airports and transit hubs. CMO Barbra Sainsurin described the approach as building an immersive "holiday world" rather than a single campaign, layering brand advertising with creator content, in-store styling events, and new shopping channels, including a partnership with DoorDash announced last month aimed at last-minute gift shoppers. Starting Friday, Anthropologie will roll out "Between Us Girls," a five-part social series on Instagram and TikTok featuring creator Coco Schiffer mixing styling tips, gift ideas and entertainment, echoing sister brand Nuuly's microdrama approach. Stores will offer free styling and concierge services in November and December, alongside new home-goods collaborations with Jon Batiste, Suleika Jaouad, New York City Ballet, Susan Alexandra, Molly Hatch and Ghia. The push follows a strong second quarter, with revenue up 5% and customer growth over 4%, as Anthropologie aims to cut through cluttered holiday marketing and drive both emotional engagement and measurable sales results amid Deloitte's forecast of 10% year-over-year holiday retail spending growth.
articles.li_summary: Anthropologie launched its "On My Way" holiday campaign, shot in Shelter Island, Mallorca and Vienna, pairing emotional reunion-themed ads with a new DoorDash delivery partnership and a five-part TikTok/Instagram series starring creator Coco Schiffer.

articles.title: YouTube tests new Shorts incentives
articles.summary: YouTube is piloting a new Shorts monetization program that invites select creators to earn bonus payments based on posting consistency and "valid, engaged Shorts views," with one example shared on X by user Muaaz showing a requirement of 16 public Shorts per month. The test currently covers invited creators in the US, UK, Germany, Brazil, Japan and South Korea, with no public application option yet, though Creator Liaison Rene Ritchie said more creators could be added in coming months. Separately, YouTube is expanding its shopping affiliate program by letting brands offer exclusive bonus commissions for videos featuring specific products, viewable through YouTube Studio's Shopping Hub, where creators can check eligible items, bonus amounts, commission rates and campaign dates. To qualify, creators must tag the product, disclose paid promotion, and keep the video public for a minimum of 30 days, though creative execution remains flexible. Additionally, YouTube rolled out upgraded shopping analytics, giving creators clearer data on content-driven sales, product click and impression performance, and seller-level breakdowns to help refine commerce strategy.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is testing a new invite-only Shorts bonus program requiring creators to post at least 16 public Shorts monthly across six countries, alongside expanded shopping affiliate bonuses and upgraded sales analytics.

articles.title: How Marriott Bonvoy got scale, speed with global creator-led campaign
articles.summary: Marriott Bonvoy debuted a new global brand platform, "Wherever life's journey takes you, we'll see you there," last month, aiming to reposition itself as a lifelong travel companion rather than just a points program. Instead of a conventional ad production process, Marriott partnered with Beautiful Destinations, a creator agency with over 50 million combined followers and a network of 650-plus creators, to shoot content across 10 countries, 15 destinations and 20 properties in only four weeks. The campaign launched in September and includes more than 1,600 out-of-home placements globally, with in-flight entertainment and OOH running through year-end and social content continuing into 2027. Marriott SVP Behnaz Ghahramani said the goal was capturing authentic, less polished moments—like rumpled sheets or mid-meal shots—rather than overproduced imagery, leaning on creators' closer audience relationships. The push targets Q4 travel mindsets, citing Nielsen data that 71% of travelers think about future trips at airports and 77% act after seeing airport ads. Bonvoy now counts over 295 million members as Marriott, which operates nearly 40 brands and 10,000-plus properties in 148 countries, prepares for its 100th anniversary in 2027.
articles.li_summary: Marriott Bonvoy launched its new global brand platform using creator agency Beautiful Destinations, producing campaign content across 10 countries, 15 destinations and 20 properties in just four weeks, with over 1,600 out-of-home placements worldwide.

articles.title: Anthropologie’s holiday marketing seeks to balance emotion, business impact
articles.summary: Anthropologie unveiled its holiday marketing strategy this week, anchored by an in-house-produced campaign called "On My Way" that depicts airport and travel-station reunions filmed on location in Shelter Island, New York, Mallorca and Vienna. The Urban Outfitters-owned retailer is treating the holidays as an immersive brand world rather than a single campaign, per Global CMO Barbra Sainsurin, layering in a five-part social series titled "Between Us Girls" starring creator Coco Schiffer, launching Friday across Instagram and TikTok with styling and gifting content. The push also activates a newly struck DoorDash partnership aimed at last-minute shoppers, in-store complimentary styling and concierge events in November and December, and home-goods collaborations with names including Suleika Jaouad, Jon Batiste, New York City Ballet, Susan Alexandra, Molly Hatch and Ghia. The strategy follows Q2 results showing 5% revenue growth and over 4% customer growth, partly credited to an earlier influencer-led fall campaign. With Deloitte projecting 10% year-over-year holiday retail spending growth driven by Gen Z and millennials, Anthropologie is betting that emotional storytelling combined with new shopping convenience will help it stand out amid heavy competition for shopper attention.
articles.li_summary: Anthropologie launched its "On My Way" holiday campaign on Monday, filmed in Shelter Island, Mallorca and Vienna, paired with a DoorDash delivery partnership and a five-part Coco Schiffer-led social series debuting Friday on Instagram and TikTok.

articles.title: What marketers need to know from Advertising Week New York 2026
articles.summary: Advertising Week New York 2026 took place over four days this month in the Penn District, bringing together thousands of marketers, agency executives and ad platform leaders for sessions, networking events and celebrity appearances, in what organizers hinted could be the event's last run at that venue. Conversations centered on several pressing industry challenges: how brands can authentically reach Gen Z and the rising Gen Alpha cohort, the shifting and still-unsettled role artificial intelligence should play in advertising workflows and creative, and whether creator marketing delivers sufficient return on investment given its growing budget share. Global president Ruth Mortimer said the event has deliberately shifted its focus toward marketers specifically because they control ad budgets, arguing that aligning with budget holders ensures the broader industry ecosystem — agencies, platforms and vendors — continues showing up. Executives from major brands including Chili's, Target, Revlon and Amazon shared perspectives during the conference, with Marketing Dive compiling its full coverage of key takeaways from these sessions for marketers who couldn't attend in person.
articles.li_summary: Advertising Week New York 2026 drew thousands of marketers to the Penn District for four days of sessions on Gen Z and Gen Alpha engagement, AI's evolving role in advertising, and creator marketing ROI, featuring executives from Chili's, Target, Revlon and Amazon.

articles.title: Meta outlines Muse AI use cases for businesses
articles.summary: Meta has shared additional use cases for its Muse AI agents aimed at small and medium-sized businesses, building on last month's launch of the Muse for SMBs package, which connects third-party tools with Muse's analytical capabilities for automated business support. According to a press release sent to SMT, the most common request from business owners is for Muse to evaluate ad campaign performance, with prompts like asking which ads perform best and why, or requesting recommendations for improvement. Another frequent use involves conversational campaign building, where owners upload creative briefs and ask Muse how to structure a Meta ads campaign using available resources. Businesses are also chaining Muse's Meta Ads connector with platforms like Shopify, Canva and HighLevel to create automated end-to-end funnels, analyzing products, determining creative direction for promotions, and then generating ads based on that strategy. Additionally, Meta noted businesses are using Muse to set up product catalogs and install pixel tracking, further streamlining operational workflows through the tool's systematic processing capabilities.
articles.li_summary: Meta detailed new Muse AI use cases for small businesses, including ad performance analysis, conversational campaign building, and automated workflows linking Meta Ads with Shopify, Canva and HighLevel for end-to-end funnels.

articles.title: YouTube tests AI replies in searches
articles.summary: YouTube is piloting an expansion of its Ask YouTube chatbot feature, moving it beyond standalone conversational queries to appear automatically atop regular search results. Previously limited to users who directly engaged the in-stream chatbot for expanded overviews and related video suggestions, Ask YouTube became available to all U.S. users last week. Now YouTube is testing surfacing AI-generated summaries at the top of standard keyword searches too, particularly for open-ended, how-to, or skill-based questions lacking a single definitive answer, such as removing marks from painted walls. Users can tap "Show more" to read the full AI response and ask follow-up questions, or scroll past it to view traditional video listings as before. YouTube frames this as adding contextual value where a structured overview helps more than a plain list of matching videos. The experiment is currently restricted to select signed-in desktop users in the U.S. browsing in English. While the feature could boost discovery and engagement, YouTube acknowledges some users may resist having AI responses inserted into every search by default.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is testing AI-generated "Ask YouTube" overviews atop all in-app search results for select signed-in U.S. desktop users searching in English, not just direct chatbot queries.

articles.title: LinkedIn adds digital business cards
articles.summary: LinkedIn is launching a new digital business card feature that lets users create a personalized, shareable version of their profile for in-person networking, with a global rollout happening over the coming months. The card displays a profile headshot, job title, and a scannable QR code, and can be saved to a user's digital wallet for quick access at events or meetings. LinkedIn is also offering multiple design and customization options, allowing users to tailor the card's appearance to reflect their personal or professional brand, as shown in images shared by Entrepreneur Editor-in-Chief Jason Feifer and developer Ishan Sharma following LinkedIn's "Connection by Design" showcase event. This isn't LinkedIn's first attempt at this concept: in 2018, the platform introduced profile QR codes for offline networking, but that feature lacked customization and never gained significant traction. With added design flexibility and wallet integration, LinkedIn is hoping this updated version will succeed where the earlier QR code tool fell short, giving professionals a more modern, engaging way to connect in real-world settings.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn is globally rolling out customizable digital business cards featuring a headshot, job title, and QR code, letting users add them to digital wallets for in-person networking.
